title: The Lamp as Spiritual Insight
english: The Spirit dances, carrying torches. Just as a torch appeared above the interpreted lamp, so also seven lamps appeared above that lamp, being a seven-fold radiance. For just as the manner of perfect luminous intellect is called seven eyes, and seven pillars support the house of wisdom, so also the seven lamps sit upon the lamp, in another manner being that which the Savior took during His visitation, soul and flesh.

For how is this whole lamp not golden, having not committed sin nor known it, upon which sit seven lamps: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of divine counsel, and strength, and knowledge, and piety, and fear of God. And how does each of these stand in relation to the one who ceased rising from the root of Jesse, having been made clear previously when it was foretold: 'A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse' (Isaiah 11:1), and the whole scope of the prophecy announcing these things.

And this seven-shining power of the seven lamps above the lamp is nourished and increases, the oil being dispensed through the seven wicks, flowing as the nourishment and guarding the light. And this is nothing other than the study of the knowledge of the truth. For from studying we bear fruit in memory and a stronger vision.

Upon all those things observed—the lamp, the torch, the seven wicks, and the lamps—two oils were also seen above the lamp, one of which was on the right and the other on the left of the torch. And see if the study concerning the intelligible things and the gifts of the Holy Spirit is oil being harvested from the oil on the right, while that concerning the world and its constitution and the providence from God is pressed from the oil on the left.

They suppose, according to a theory, to say another, an oil being on the right of the torch, to be the theory concerning the Only-begotten Son of God, the one on the left nourishing the Word concerning the incarnation. For this one also shines, but not in the same way as the theory on the right and preceding. I once heard a teacher leading the Catholic Church clarifying the presented word, that the torch above the lamp is the...

The light is the illumination of the Father, and the oils on the right and from the good-smelling ones are the words concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit. But he did not provide this interpretation, bearing this meaning, as to how one thing is on the right and the other is from the good-smelling ones.

Since the present theory concerning the lamp is not a sensible but a mental one, see whether this is not that which Moses saw on the mountain according to the pattern shown to him, and not another being of the so-called idea; toward the invisible and mental lamp the sensible one was constructed according to the description of the hierophant Moses.

It is not untimely to write alongside the things seen and that which was said in the Gospel by Jesus: 'No one,' he says, 'having lit a lamp, puts it in a hidden place or under a vessel or a bed, but on the lamp, so that all those in the house may see the light' (Matt 5:15).

It is possible in these things to take the house to be the Church of the living God, becoming His house, in which those remaining and dwelling, standing according to its doctrines, are illuminated toward the lamp placed by the lamp, which is snatched away by the one educating those traversing in the house of God according to the statutes and canons and doctrines of the ecclesiastical opinion. And this teacher illuminates when he lifts up his own mind like a lamp, which he does not hide under a bed or vessel, but places upon his spoken word, being allegorically addressed as a lamp, having 'a tongue of instruction' as it must be said.

It is also possible to call the practical life a lamp, upon which the enlightened mind of the one who has enlightened himself with the light of knowledge rests. Let him who is urging on the present clarity of the existing prophetic word examine whether it is necessary to receive it or to seek another from those... having stepped into understanding. For thus an exactified intellect comes to bear fruit.

'And I asked and said to the angel speaking in me, saying, What are these, Lord? And the angel speaking in me answered and said to me, saying, This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might nor by power, but by my spirit, says the Lord of all' (Zech 4:6). The prophet says he asked the angel speaking in him, desiring to learn what the divine things shown to him were.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of Christ and the Mountain of the Lord
english: Visions, that is, all things revealed, or those specifically preceding the present word, which is about the whole golden lampstand and the things upon it: a lamp, seven small lamps, and equal lamps, and two olives, one on the right and the other on the left of the lamp.

Regarding the question of whether these are not perceived by the senses, the one asked immediately answered that they are the word of God from the person of Zerubbabel, from which it appears that the things shown were intellectual visions and that this is true. The showing of the revealed things happened to the prophet while he was still in Babylon, in which neither the house of God was built, nor the vessels in it, of which the lampstand and the things upon it are. Since these are thus viewed, one must remain with the interpretation spoken of them or seek something greater than it.
The word which... the angel said to the prophet was not done by great power or by the strength of man or of any other creature, but in the Spirit of the Lord it was spoken and was revealed.

The Holy Spirit of the Lord is continually called so in the Scriptures, as also in other Scriptures besides the present one. Concerning Him, a lament and that in Isaiah is announced thus: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me' (Isaiah 61:1). In agreement with these, the apostle Paul, writing to the Corinthians, says: 'For what man knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God, which searches even the mystic depths of God' (1 Corinthians 2:11). And again in Isaiah, the Originator and Provider of all things says: 'A Spirit shall go out from me' (Isaiah 59:19).

By this Spirit, the things shown before the person of Zerubbabel were revealed, but not by great power or strength of any creature. For there is another power provided with the Spirit to those worthy, about which the Savior, in the Acts of the Apostles, says to his disciples, as he was being taken up into heaven to his Father: 'You shall receive power upon the coming of the Holy Spirit' (Acts 1:8). Correspondingly, at the end of the Gospel according to Luke, the Savior, ascending from where he came, having given the Holy Spirit to the apostles, says: 'But you shall sit in the city...'

"...until you are clothed with power from on high." This power is not a different power from that of Christ, who is "the wisdom and power of God," from which the evangelical preaching has surpassed the apostles, one of whom, Paul, writes: "My speech and my preaching are not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in a demonstration of Spirit and power" (1 Cor 2:4), which is sometimes provided by God who has stretched out His hand, as it is said concerning John in the Gospel, "having gone before the Lord in spirit and power" (Luke 1:80).

Understand precisely if the thing announced to Mary by the holy angel Gabriel has the same understanding: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you" (Luke 1:35). In the mentioned Spirit of God, in the words set forth and many others, the announcement has occurred before Zerubbabel and the power joined with him, "and not by any other great power and might" (Zech 4:7). For this is inferior, even if it be divine and highly esteemed.

Who are you, O great mountain before Zerubbabel, to level the stone of the inheritance to be equal to its grace (Zech 4:7)? As a logical and understandable approach to a divine voice through speech, either the discerning prophet or the angel speaking in him approaches. What is it that he says to him? Who are you, O mountain standing before Zerubbabel to level, and who is the stone which I will make equal to the inheritance by grace? Regarding these things, whoever says the two designations exist in parallel concerning the visiting Savior. For many scriptures name him both mountain and stone.

For in "The mountain of the Lord shall be made manifest at the end of days" (Isa 2:2), the Son of God is, concerning whom He spoke at the end of days after speaking through Moses and the prophets. Of Him also it is demonstrative: "Ascend the mountain of Zion, O evangelizer, Zion" (Isa 2:3). And there are ten thousand other testimonies concerning this, which the present writer should refrain from passing over, lest the word become too much beyond what is necessary, especially since often the things concerning the mountain being the Savior have been interpreted in the commentaries of the divine Psalms and of the...

title: The Mountain and the Stone
english: Regarding the final vision of Isaiah. Even the named mountain, Savior, is called a stone in the saying: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner' (Ps 118:22). Remembering this word in the Acts of the Apostles, the preeminent disciple of the Savior, Peter, most strictly rebuked the Pharisees, scribes, and Sadducees who were listening to the Jewish teaching, saying: 'This is the stone which was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner' (Acts 4:11).

And since it is not only the head of the divine building but also the foundation, God promises concerning it, saying: 'Behold, I lay a cornerstone in the foundations of Zion, chosen, precious, upon which the believer has unashamed hope' (Isa 28:16). Laying out these words, Peter, the disciple of Christ, upon whom the Church is built, exhorts and advises those to whom he has inscribed his epistle: 'To whom approaching the living stone, you are being built up into a spiritual house in which spiritual sacrifices are offered' (1 Pet 2:5).

Of what inheritance does the stone belong? It is of that inheritance concerning which it is brought forth in Isaiah: 'There is an inheritance to those healing the Lord' (Isa 35:10), and of that inheritance concerning which the hymnodist said, singing: 'My inheritance is most strong for me; you are the one restoring my inheritance to me' (Ps 16:5).

See then whether the stone is the inheritance of that inheritance being fulfilled from the God-fearing ones according to each, which is chosen and desired, existing from the cause of all things, according to that which was announced by the spirit-bearing men, apostles and evangelists, prophets and the great high priest of all things, Moses: 'He chose for us his own inheritance,' God, clearly, 'the beauty of Jacob whom he loved' (Jer 31:3).

It is equal to the voice from the Psalm and that in the great song of Deuteronomy having here: 'Jacob became a part of the Lord, a portion of his inheritance, Israel' (Deut 33:9). But especially the stone being hymned is the inheritance of that which is signified in the second Psalm toward this stone: 'The Lord said to me, Son are you, I have today become your father. Ask of me and I will give you nations for your inheritance' (Ps 2:7-8).
Toward the assigned theory, the mountain and the stone from parallel...

Regarding how it is to be carried, it must be said and otherwise that one part is the mountain and another part is the stone. And the mountain of achievement is the unwedded Mary; but the stone coming forth from her, whom she bore as a son without a man, exists. The book of the most wise Daniel initiates us into these mysteries.

For it has been said in it that the striking stone—the various kingdoms and the image completed from them—has been cut and torn away from it without the custom and the practiced way toward the generation of the energy from parents. For as many as have the generation from both parents, they are torn and cut away from the hands of the marriage acts and from those who conceive; but only the one born from the virgin, not knowing the man, has been torn away and cut from her without hands. Before the face of Zerubbabel, it happened that the stone from the mountain was to be cut without hands, so that Jesus is also traced through lineage from it. It is interpreted, therefore, as 'a movement of a flow' because the customary flow of parents is moved, by a virgin alone without a man being brought to pass.

But the stone placed outside of the inheritance has grace upon grace, according to the thought of what the Baptist John said, 'for from the fullness we have all received' (John 1:16). For the whole visitation of the Savior and the salvation upon it happened by grace, as the theologian says to those whom he addresses in his epistle: 'You are saved by grace, and this is not from us, but the gift of God' (Ephesians 2:8). [Zechariah 4:8-9: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall complete it, and he shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you.]

The prophecy of the seen house is not spoken concerning a sensible building. For it has already been said that this prophet, while still in Babylon, with the seventieth year of the captivity already having come, was initiated into the placed revelations. But not in Babylon, but in Jerusalem and after the captivity, the sensible house was built. Therefore, the present voice does not happen to be about it; for as if concerning the temple being present and already having come, it is said pointedly about it: 'This house.'
